what_happened: Planning read found that the module docstring claim 'hmarkers holds at colourFibre D for every D' is false as literally stated: hmarkers quantifies over ALL TaskModels of the frame, and a valuation making markerAtom false everywhere refutes it. The claim is true only under the intended marker valuation. The plan therefore adds a fixed-model variant of the reduction theorem plus a markerModel definition, and requires correcting two docstrings, rather than discharging the existing all-models hypothesis.

Task description names 'the probes/ file' as the consumer, but the probe content has since landed in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/OpenFutureUndefinable.lean and specs/ROADMAP.md line 228 directs re-pointing scope at the landed module. Plan targets the landed module and declares the 859 probe out of scope.

The 'instance-unification blocker' turned out to be a one-line asymmetry found in minutes: FrameOver.translationProduct states its own @[simp] _taskRel bridge in the same file, colourClock does not. No research dispatch was needed; targeted reads of TranslationProduct.lean, TaskFrame.lean and PartialHistory.lean grounded the whole plan.

colourClock_taskRel closed on the first rung of the plan's mitigation ladder: a bare 'FrameOver.ofReflectiveRegular_taskRel' term, with no haveI, no show, and no reflect_restrict_iff fallback. The Nonempty (W x D) instance baked into colourClock's body unified with the lemma's instance-implicit argument by postponed instance unification, exactly as translationProduct_taskRel already does.

git-commit-scoped.sh refused the phase-1 commit on typst-sync-check.sh Check 2: typst/generated/status.typ's formalsystem-line-count was 15 lines stale, exactly the size of this phase's edit. Fixed forward with 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix' and added typst/generated/status.typ to the phase's staged path list. Consequence for later phases: every Lean-line-count-changing phase in this plan must regenerate and stage that file, which the plan's Files-to-modify lists do not name.

colourFibre_hmarkers' pinned signature names its hypothesis binder 'hm', but the hypothesis is genuinely unused (a marker-future witness exists at every (tau,t) of colourFibre, marker bit or not), so Lean's unusedVariables linter emitted a warning that the phase's own 'no warning' verification criterion forbids. Renamed the binder to '_hm'; the hypothesis TYPE and the proposition proved are unchanged, and the docstring now records why the binder is underscored.

scripts/check-module-invariants.sh C16 flagged the new @[simp] colourClock_taskRel with 'LINTER FAILED: maximum recursion depth'. Root cause: Batteries' simpNF env_linter adds every Prop-valued non-instance hypothesis of the lemma under test to the simp set ('simp [*]', so a conditional simp lemma can apply to itself), and colourClock_taskRel's hR hypothesis is the reflection condition R w d u <-> R u (-d) w, an unconditional rewrite loop once neg_neg closes the cycle. The linter aborts before reaching any normal-form verdict. The declaration cannot conform (colourClock takes its four conditions as explicit args; isCondition exempts only instance-implicit binders), so the repo's documented permanent-exemption route was used: @[simp, nolint simpNF] with the reason at the site plus a scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt entry, which C26 then verified (9 pairs, PASS). Not anticipated by the plan.

scripts/check-module-invariants.sh exits 1 for a PRE-EXISTING C16 unusedArguments finding on FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderChain.lean:2136 (mem_cellAt_of_shift_of_hasForwardSlack, argument 23). Not caused by this task: the file's working tree is clean and its last commit is task 850's, several commits before this task's first. It is sibling task 889's own subject ('ladderchain_c16_unusedarguments_clear', file scope LadderChain.lean + scripts/nolints.json), so it is outside this task's territory and was left untouched. Consequence: Phase 4's 'check-module-invariants.sh exits 0' criterion is unreachable in this dispatch; C2, C14, C20 and C26 all pass.

lean-plan-compliance-check.sh returned COMPLIANCE_CHECK: failed on four names, all false negatives of its grep heuristic, which requires a declaration line to START with the keyword. colourClock_taskRel exists at TranslationProduct.lean:321 but is written '@[simp, nolint simpNF] theorem colourClock_taskRel', which the regex cannot match; hmarkers and hinexpr are hypothesis binder names, not declarations; 'm' is the marker atom's prose name in the Goals block. Recorded as failed in return-meta with a per-name disposition rather than laundered to passed, and status left implemented. Suggested script fix: allow an optional leading '@[...]' attribute block in the per-name grep.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #860's declared file_scope.
